summary: Across 8 units the content is accurate and conservative. Every numeric key was recomputed in Python and matches: Cockcroft-Gault 41.6 and 34.4 mL/min, breakthrough 30 mg, oral to SC morphine 2:1 (90 to 45, 150 to 75), adjusted calcium 3.16, frailty index 0.25 and 0.40, postural drops 29 and 32, ACB 7 and 8, NNT 25, Barthel 55 and 75. The lessons teach no unhedged doses. The opioid ratios (oral to SC morphine 2:1, breakthrough one-tenth to one-sixth) match standard PCF and NICE practice and are repeatedly hedged to current references, with renal impairment, incomplete cross-tolerance and arithmetic double-checking all covered. Capacity, ADRT, LPA, IMCA, DNACPR/ReSPECT, NG249, NG234 24-hour MRI, CFS 4-7 anchors, STOPP/START and ACB thresholds are correct. No critical or major problems were found. The few minor issues are one Barthel banding label, one explanation that misreads a Barthel item, a withdrawn drug used in an example, and some scope gaps. No tab or control characters, literal unicode escape text, '[object Object]', placeholder steps or stale option references were found. NICE CG140 currency was not checked against the live NICE site. This is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert (palliative medicine and geriatrics) before clinical reliance.

issues.problem: Worked example states a Barthel total of 55/100 'indicates moderate dependence'. Common banding (Shah) places 21-60 as severe dependency and 61-90 as moderate; q003 (75, 'mild to moderate') is consistent only with a moderate band. Banding varies by source and was not verified against a single reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Say the total shows 'substantial (severe on common banding) dependence', or cite the banding used and note that bands vary, rather than asserting 'moderate'.

issues.problem: Explanation says 'the lowest items (dressing, bathing, stairs) suggest goals for therapy'. In the standard Barthel, bathing is scored 0 or 5, so bathing 5 is the maximum (independent) score and not a deficit. Dressing 0 and stairs 5 (of 10) are the real losses.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to 'the items below maximum (dressing 0/10, stairs 5/10, toilet use 5/10, mobility 10/15) suggest goals for therapy'. Drop bathing.

issues.problem: The example uses ranitidine (ACB score 1), which has been unavailable in the UK since the 2019-20 recall. A UK clinical-year student may be misled about current prescribing.
issues.suggestedFix: Substitute a currently available drug with ACB 1 (for example warfarin, as in the lesson example, or metoprolol or codeine) and recompute. Keep the total at 8 only if the scores are kept consistent.

issues.problem: The unit title and lesson cover delirium (including the 4AT) but none of the three objectives mention it and no question tests it. Objective 3 (pressure ulcer prevention and harms of immobility) has only two MCQs plus one theory item.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a delirium objective and at least one question (4AT features, or hypoactive delirium recognition), or remove delirium from the title and lesson focus.

issues.problem: Objective 2 lists constipation and agitation but no question tests constipation management. The lesson also teaches only oral to SC morphine 2:1, with no mention that UK end-of-life practice commonly uses SC diamorphine (oral morphine to SC diamorphine about 3:1 per PCF, unverified here) even though the warning callout cites morphine/diamorphine mix-ups. Named anticipatory drugs (hyoscine for secretions, midazolam, levomepromazine) are not taught.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one constipation question. Add a hedged sentence that diamorphine is also used SC and has a different ratio to be checked in the PCF/BNF. Optionally name the standard anticipatory drug classes without doses.
